To start, I'm a guy, 5'4". So I'm pretty short, but there's nothing I can do about that. That plays a part later on in this retail tale.

I work in one of the major retail stores. Generally, I'm not a cashier, but a few called out today, so I was brought to the front to ring. I do have the personality for being a salesman, but I don't have the personality for cashiering at all. The customers act like you're their personal slave and it drives me nuts.

I was put on the express line. You know, the line that's 14 items or less but you could get away with 20 or so.

A 600-pound woman rolls up to the register with her basket PACKED and overflowing with make-up. She starts dropping armfuls on the counter. According to the receipt I saw after, she had 112 items. 112. In an express lane. The customers behind her had comments for her, but she ignored them. They were mostly just moaning and groaning while the butterhuffer loaded up the counter.

We are NOT allowed to say anything to customers who do this, so I kept my mouth shut and hoped she could feel my silent judgment as I scanned the shit she was going to use to try to make her face look less like a moon later.

"Speed up, shorty," she said, smacking her lips.

I looked right at her and said "don't call me that."

She laughed. "I can call you whatever the fuck you want."

"Okay, fatty." I couldn't stop myself.

Her face turned red as a tomato (large pepperoni pizza?) and she shut her trap. She said absolutely nothing for the rest of the transaction and promptly sped off in her scooter at the end. I was positive she was going to report me but nothing came of it, probably because she was embarrassed someone said that to her.

I don't regret it.
